tasks.objective: Add bounded retry with backoff to the artifact export worker.

transcript.text: The artifact export worker fails permanently on the first transient storage error. Add bounded retry with backoff.
Read src/powercontext/builtin/export/worker.py. The drain loop calls storage.delete once and lets StorageUnavailable escape.
grep -n StorageUnavailable src/powercontext/builtin/export/worker.py -> 41: raise StorageUnavailable(entry_id)
The scope already ships a retry helper used by the capture queue.
read src/powercontext/builtin/runtime/backoff.py -> def run_with_backoff(operation, deadline_seconds, delays)
First pass: reuse run_with_backoff with a 30 second base and no jitter.
A 30 second base is far too slow here. The export worker drains every 5 seconds.
Revised choice: the retry base is 1 second with full jitter, sized to the 5 second drain interval.
read tests/builtin/export/test_worker.py -> 12 tests, none assert retry behaviour
Proposed adding a new retry dependency so the delay table becomes declarative.
No new dependency. The core dependency set stays minimal; use the existing helper.
Putting the retry around the whole drain call would double-count the attempt when the worker restarts.
run pytest tests/builtin/export/test_worker.py -> 12 passed in 0.42s
The drain loop already owns restart recovery, so the retry must live inside the loop body and stay in memory only.

required_state_facts.text: the export worker drains on a 5 second interval
the helper to reuse is run_with_backoff in src/powercontext/builtin/runtime/backoff.py
the retry base is 1 second with full jitter
no new dependency may be added
retry stays in memory because the drain loop already owns restart recovery
tests/builtin/export/test_worker.py does not assert retry behaviour yet

expected_next_action.text: call run_with_backoff with a 1 second base and full jitter inside the drain loop body, then add a retry regression test in the export worker test module

known_omissions: The maximum attempt count for the drain loop was never agreed.
No test covers a storage outage longer than one drain interval.

tasks.objective: Make the lease expiry test deterministic instead of time-dependent.

transcript.text: The lease expiry test fails roughly one run in five. Make it deterministic.
Reproduced it 4 times in 20 runs. The test sleeps for the lease duration and then asserts the claim is gone.
read tests/unit/test_leases.py -> test_expired_lease_is_not_claimable sleeps 1.2 seconds against a 1.0 second lease
The store takes lease_duration as a timedelta, so the test can inject a very short lease instead of sleeping.
read src/powercontext_eval/web/store.py -> class TaskStore(lease_duration: timedelta)
Root cause: the suite asserts on wall-clock expiry, so scheduler jitter decides the outcome.
Do not add a shared time abstraction just for one test.
Rejected option: raise the sleep to 5 seconds, which would hide the flake instead of removing it.
run pytest tests/unit/test_leases.py -q --count 20 -> 3 failures
The failing runs all lose the race between the sleep and the second claim attempt.
Fix it without changing production behaviour and without a new abstraction.
Chosen fix: construct the store with a lease_duration of a few milliseconds and assert on the returned claim result, not on elapsed time.

TaskStore accepts lease_duration as a timedelta, so a short lease can be injected
the root cause is asserting on wall-clock expiry rather than on the returned claim result
adding a shared time abstraction for this test was rejected
raising the sleep duration was rejected as hiding the flake
production behaviour must not change

expected_next_action.text: construct TaskStore with a millisecond lease_duration in tests/unit/test_leases.py and assert on the returned claim result instead of elapsed time
